claims: On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong became the first human to step on the Moon.
Neil Armstrong stepped on the Moon during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.
Neil Armstrong declared "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind".
The Apollo 11 mission landed in the Sea of Tranquility.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin spent over 21 hours on the Moon's surface.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin conducted a 2.5-hour walk on the Moon's surface.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin collected 21.5 kg of material from the Moon.
Neil Armstrong stepped onto the lunar surface at 10:56 p.m. EDT.
Neil Armstrong manually piloted the Lunar Module Eagle to a safe landing spot 6 km from the intended site.
The Lunar Module Eagle landed with seconds of fuel remaining.
Apollo 11 fulfilled the US national goal of landing men on the Moon and returning them safely.
Apollo 11 effectively won the space race against the Soviet Union.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin left behind an American flag on the Moon.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin left behind a patch honoring the Apollo 1 crew on the Moon.
Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin left behind a gold olive branch pin on the Moon.
Neil Armstrong retired from NASA in 1971.
Neil Armstrong taught aerospace engineering at the University of Cincinnati.
Neil Armstrong passed away on August 25, 2012.
